title: Do a reimbursement deadline and delayed-payment interest start on the same event?

conversation.text: They paid my reimbursement claim on 26 August. I submitted it on 1 August and uploaded the last document on 5 August. Does interest start after 15 days from upload?
When did the insurer receive the last necessary document, and did it confirm that no other necessary document remained? Uploading to the adviser does not establish insurer receipt.
Its acknowledgement says 7 August, and it confirms that this was the last necessary document. Payment of 100000 arrived on 26 August.

The cited wording gives two anchors: noncashless settlement within 15 days from claim submission, and delayed-payment interest from receipt of the last necessary document to actual payment. Preserve 1 August submission, 5 August upload, 7 August insurer receipt and 26 August payment separately. The elapsed submission interval is 25 days and the stated receipt-to-payment interval is 19 days. Those intervals are not an interest amount: the dated bank rate, day-count and rounding authority remain missing.

expected_answer: Apply the two clauses separately. The stated payment is more than 15 days after submission. Under the cited delayed-payment clause, the last necessary-document insurer receipt is the interest anchor, not adviser upload and not automatically the end of the settlement deadline. Bank Rate is the RBI rate prevalent on the first day of the financial year in which the claim fell due: for the August 2026 fixture, obtain the relevant 1 April 2026 rate. Add two percentage points, not two percent of that rate. Do not invent the monetary interest result or equate a file-count/upload marker with documentary completeness.
acceptable_alternatives: Equivalent conditional date and trigger explanation with precise missing inputs.
